newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-KADLEC RETURNS TO SHORE UP CZECH DEFENCE AGAINST SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KADLEC RETURNS TO SHORE UP CZECH DEFENCE AGAINST SPAIN.

text.p: Czech coach Dusan Uhrin brought back veteran defender Miroslav Kadlec to bolster his back line when he named his squad on Tuesday for next week's World Cup qualifier against Spain.

Kadlec, 32, who plays for German club Kaiserslautern, has been plagued by an Achilles tendon injury recently and missed the Czechs' 6-0 drubbing of Malta in their first European group six qualifier in September.
But Uhrin said that after watching Kadlec play in a German second division match at the weekend he had little doubt the defender would be ready for the match in Prague on October 9.
"I watched him play in the Cup Winners' Cup and then last Sunday against Leipzig and he played well," Uhrin said.
Uhrin said he was, for the most part, leaving intact the team which reached the final of this year's European championship.
Only three of the 19 players named for the Spain match were not in the squad which provided the side which finished runners-up to Germany in Euro 96.
They are Sparta Prague defender Tomas Repka, midfielder Richard Dostalek of Boby Brno and forward Radovan Hromadko of FK Jablonec.

Uhrin also moved quickly to dispel rumours that he would replace his number one goalkeeper Petr Kouba, who has seen little action since he was transferred to Spain's Deportivo La Coruna from Sparta Prague at the beginning of the season.

Uhrin rejected the suggestion that he might put Pavel Srnicek of English premier league Newcastle in the starting line-up instead of Kouba, saying Kouba was well suited to facing Spain, "especially since we will be playing at Sparta stadium".
Kadlec's Kaiserslautern team mate Pavel Kuka and Vladimir Smicer of French first division Lens will lead the attack.
But Uhrin said he expected English-based midfielders Patrik Berger and Karel Poborsky, dubbed "the dynamic duo" by the home press, to join almost every attack.
Goalkeepers - Petr Kouba (Deportivo La Coruna, Spain), Pavel Srnicek (Newcastle United, England)
Defenders - Miroslav Kadlec (Kaiserslautern, Germany), Lubos Kubik (Slavia Prague), Tomas Repka (Sparta Prague), Michal Hornak (Sparta Prague), Jan Suchoparek (Strasbourg, France)

Midfielders - Radoslav Latal (Schalke, Germany), Jiri Nemec (Schalke, Germany), Karel Poborsky (Manchester United, England), Pavel Nedved (Lazio, Italy), Patrik Berger (Liverpool, England), Radek Bejbl (Atletico Madrid, Spain), Pavel Novotny (Slavia Prague), Martin Frydek (Sparta Prague), Richard Dostalek (Boby Brno)
Attackers - Pavel Kuka (Kaiserslautern, Germany), Vladimir Smicer (Lens, France), Radovan Hromadko (FK Jablonec).
